# GUI ↔ CLI ↔ SNMP Mapping — Juniper (Junos) EX/QFX Series

Per [gui-cli-snmp-unification.md](../../00-architecture/gui-cli-snmp-unification.md), every GUI action must be traceable to literal CLI text echoed into the terminal. For Junos, **every config-changing row below ends in a `commit` line that must appear as its own distinct, visible terminal entry** — a GUI "Apply" is not complete, and has had zero effect on the device, until that line succeeds. This is the one structural difference from every other vendor's mapping file in this doc set; see [overview.md](overview.md) for why.

| GUI Action | CLI as echoed in terminal | SNMP SET (MIB::object, OID) | Read-back / GUI sync source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enable port | `configure`<br>`delete interfaces ge-0/0/1 disable`<br>`commit` | **None.** `IF-MIB::ifAdminStatus` (`1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.7`) is explicitly documented as not SET-able on Junos. | `show interfaces ge-0/0/1 terse` (admin/link column); `IF-MIB::ifOperStatus` GET for read-only confirmation. | No SNMP fallback exists for this vendor — always requires a live CLI session. Re-enabling is a `delete` of the `disable` statement, not a positive `enable` statement. |
| Disable port | `configure`<br>`set interfaces ge-0/0/1 disable`<br>`commit` | **None** (same restriction as above). | Same as above. | Same no-SNMP-fallback caveat. |
| Set port description | `configure`<br>`set interfaces ge-0/0/1 description "Uplink to core-sw1 Gi1/0/24"`<br>`commit` | `IF-MIB::ifAlias` (`1.3.6.1.2.1.31.1.1.1.18`) — **not separately confirmed as writable on Junos** in this research pass; do not assume it works without testing against the target platform/release. | `show configuration interfaces ge-0/0/1` or `IF-MIB::ifAlias` GET. | Treat CLI as the only confirmed path; verify SNMP write empirically before relying on it as a fallback. |
| Configure access VLAN on a port | `configure`<br>`set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family ethernet-switching interface-mode access`<br>`set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family ethernet-switching vlan members staff`<br>`commit` | `Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qVlanStaticEgressPorts` / `dot1qVlanStaticUntaggedPorts` (`1.3.6.1.2.1.46.1.3.1.1.4`/`.1.3.6.1.2.1.46.1.3.1.1.5`) — **not confirmed reliable for SET on Junos EX**; field reports describe inconsistent NMS support and ELS-platform differences. | `show vlans staff detail`; `Q-BRIDGE-MIB::dot1qVlanStaticTable` GET (read path is reliable even where write is not). | CLI is the only path to treat as dependable; do not build an SNMP-SET fallback for this action without platform-specific verification. |
| Configure trunk VLANs on a port | `configure`<br>`set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family ethernet-switching interface-mode trunk`<br>`set interfaces ge-0/0/1 unit 0 family ethernet-switching vlan members [ staff guests eng ]`<br>`commit` | Same uncertainty as access-VLAN row above. | Same as above. | |
| Enable RSTP edge on a port | `configure`<br>`set protocols rstp interface ge-0/0/1 edge`<br>`commit` | **None found.** No standard or Juniper enterprise MIB object for STP edge-port administrative configuration was located. | `show spanning-tree interface ge-0/0/1`; `BRIDGE-MIB::dot1dStpPortTable` GET (state only, not the edge-port admin setting itself). | CLI-only action. |
| Configure LACP / aggregated-Ethernet membership | `configure`<br>`set chassis aggregated-devices ethernet device-count 5`<br>`set interfaces ge-0/0/1 ether-options 802.3ad ae0`<br>`set interfaces ae0 aggregated-ether-options lacp active`<br>`commit` | **None found.** No confirmed MIB object for SNMP-driven LAG-membership configuration on Junos. | `show lacp interfaces ae0`; `show interfaces ae0 terse`. | Note the two-step nature (chassis-wide `device-count` reservation, then per-member assignment) — both lines must be echoed if `device-count` hasn't already been raised for the target `ae` index. |
| Configure port security (MAC limiting) | `configure`<br>`set ethernet-switching-options secure-access-port interface ge-0/0/1 mac-limit 4 action drop`<br>`commit` | **None found.** No Juniper enterprise MIB object located for port-security configuration writes. | `show configuration ethernet-switching-options secure-access-port`; `show ethernet-switching interfaces ge-0/0/1 detail`. | CLI-only action. |
| **Save/commit configuration** | `commit` (plain), or `commit confirmed 5` for auto-rollback safety, or `commit check` for dry-run validation only | **N/A — not an SNMP concept on Junos.** There is no SNMP-SET equivalent of "commit the candidate config"; JUNIPER-CFGMGMT-MIB only emits read-only *notifications about* a commit that already happened via CLI/NETCONF. | `show system commit` (rollback/commit history); `show configuration` (post-commit active config) for full-state confirmation. | **This is the row that most differs from every other vendor's mapping file.** A GUI "Apply"/"Save" button must issue this as its own visible terminal line, separate from and after the `set` lines — never silently folded into the action. Default SignalScope behavior should be `commit confirmed <N>` for any change touching interface/management reachability, with the GUI surfacing the confirm window and requiring an explicit follow-up confirm (or auto-rollback) — see [overview.md](overview.md). |
| Configure SNMP community | `configure`<br>`set snmp community public authorization read-only`<br>`set snmp community public clients 10.0.0.0/24`<br>`commit` | `SNMP-COMMUNITY-MIB::snmpCommunityTable` — **confirmed SET-able** per Junos's own SNMP FAQ (one of the few objects explicitly documented as writable). | `show configuration snmp`; `SNMP-COMMUNITY-MIB::snmpCommunityTable` GET. | One of the rare Junos config actions where an SNMP-SET fallback is actually documented as viable — but only relevant for a device already reachable via a pre-existing read-write community, which is a bootstrapping chicken-and-egg problem in practice (you need write SNMP access to configure SNMP access). CLI/NETCONF remains the realistic path for first-time setup. |
| Configure SNMP trap target | `configure`<br>`set snmp trap-group ops-traps version v2 targets 10.0.0.50`<br>`commit` (v1/v2c); SNMPv3 requires the longer `vacm`/`target-address`/`target-parameters`/`notify` chain — see [cli-reference.md](cli-reference.md) | **None found** for trap-group/target-address configuration itself. | `show configuration snmp`. | CLI-only action, including for the more elaborate SNMPv3 notification chain. |

## Summary takeaway for SignalScope's Junos implementation

Across every switch-configuration action researched (port state, description, VLAN, STP, LACP, port security), **no confirmed, reliable SNMP-SET path exists** — the only genuinely SNMP-writable objects found are SNMP-agent self-configuration (community strings) and a handful of generic system scalars/RMON control objects, none of which are switch-port configuration. Combined with the candidate-config/commit model, this means Junos is functionally **CLI-only (or NETCONF-only) for configuration changes** in SignalScope's architecture, with SNMP relegated to read-only polling/read-back — a sharper version of the "SNMP write coverage is inconsistent and narrow" pattern called out generally in [gui-cli-snmp-unification.md](../../00-architecture/gui-cli-snmp-unification.md#handling-vendor-asymmetry).
